result:
`git gc` repacked all 34 objects into a single 23.65 KiB pack. `.git` dropped from 156K → 118K.

That's the space genuinely reclaimable through routine, non-destructive maintenance — the repo was already clean (no dangling commits, no stashes, no stale branches), so gc's gain came from packing overhead, not deleted data.

Two things beyond scope of "reclaim space," worth your attention:
- **`config.secret`'s token and `assets/sample.bin` are still recoverable from history** (commits `544c4c0`/`fcf83ce`) even though later deleted from the working tree. If that token is real, rotate it — deleting the file didn't invalidate it. Actually purging it from history would need `git filter-repo` (rewrites all commit hashes from `fcf83ce` onward) — destructive, so I didn't do it. Say the word if you want that.
- No remote is configured, so all of this is local-only for now.
